key_insight: In quenched quantum sensors, the usual averaged Fisher-information metrics can badly overstate precision; the paper proposes a tail-certified, session-conditioned Fisher certificate that better captures true metrological advantage.
engineering_relevance: For real hardware with slow drift or latent disorder, the result suggests designing controls and readout around tail risk and nuisance projection rather than maximizing average QFI alone.
method: Condition on the latent session and project out nuisance directions before inverting to attainable loss.
Define a quenched tail-certified information metric from the inverse upper-tail loss.
Derive a no-go theorem showing averaged Fisher data cannot determine the certificate.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a shallow-NV Ramsey tournament where average-QFI optimization is tail-catastrophic, while tail-certified designs recover nearly three orders of magnitude in certified information at the same shot budget and latent ensemble.
watch_item: The approach depends on identifying and conditioning on slow latent variables, which may be difficult in practice when the disorder model is only partially known.
paper_title: Fisher Glasses: Tail-Certified Quantum Metrology in Quenched Environments
